reviewType: AI-assisted rubric review; no human or clinical validation
method: Original generated outputs were reviewed before edits. Both validation-failed runs remain in the denominator and their content is reviewed.
Each output item is split into substantive atomic claims; repeated claims count again where repeated. Pure questions without factual premises are excluded.
Attached source passages are checked for meaning, independently of mechanical reference validity. Canonical quotes were resolved by the server, not authored by the model.

Bounded absence claims can use all declared scopeDocumentIds as evidence. These are labeled document-scope and are reported separately from passage-cited claims. A missing scope document is a validation failure even when the bounded absence is true in the selected records.

No confirmation/no documentation phrasing is treated as an evidence-status claim. Assertions that a person did not acknowledge, a response was not received, or a discussion never happened are event claims and are not established merely by absent documentation.

Reports presented as verified world facts and disputed plans stated as settled are partially supported and flagged as source-wide unsupported certainty; this is an explicit conservative adjudication choice.
A conflict category itself conveys a disagreement; categorizing a compatible plan or documentation gap as conflict is reviewed as an additional unsupported classification claim.
Expected-item coverage requires meaningful qualifiers and details. A task to confirm something may partially cover a gap but does not fully state its documentation status.

highestConsequenceFindings.issue: Documented uncertainty is converted into claims about what happened.
examples: straightforward-1 item-2: Mira has not acknowledged this pickup time.
straightforward-2 item-3: Mira has not acknowledged this pickup time.
missing-2 item-7: no response received yet.
highestConsequenceFindings.whyItMatters: The reviewer may treat an undocumented event as a known failure to act; valid references and canonical passages do not prevent the inference.

highestConsequenceFindings.issue: Disputed discharge-plan details appear as settled in the leading situation item.
highestConsequenceFindings.whyItMatters: Both versions appear later, but a reviewer scanning the opening may take the initial appointment and support version as established.

highestConsequenceFindings.issue: Compatible documentation gaps are labeled as conflicts.
highestConsequenceFindings.whyItMatters: False conflict labels create unnecessary reconciliation work. The latter also fails structural validation.

highestConsequenceFindings.issue: Important facts and gaps disappear despite complete valid references.
examples: Both conflicting runs omit copied/nonindependent source provenance and unsuccessful outreach.
missing-1 omits blank event dates; missing-2 omits missing admission date and export-versus-event warning.
highestConsequenceFindings.whyItMatters: The evaluator must measure content coverage independently of reference integrity.

limitations: Six runs over three authored fictional cases; not an estimate of real-world reliability.
AI-assisted adjudication contains judgment calls about atomic claim boundaries and attribution strength.
